record.reply_text:
Your Emacs stepper is on the right session now, so the T4 reload took effect. But it holds 35 frames and isn't getting new ones. Checking Emacs's messages for stepper errors (read-only):㊥ (gist) Fixed in code (futon3c `969de94d6`). The Emacs stepper will now catch up on its own and stay level with the web page. It needs one reload of `~/code/futon3c/emacs/turn-stepper.el` in your Emacs. Your Emacs's "Stack hot reload" didn't pick this change up: the new functions aren't defined there yet.

㊢ ("the stepper window is still stuck") It wasn't frozen; it was dropping turns. Your Emacs stepper had 35 frames against the web page's 36. It was missing your 02:27 turn ("Yes, please restart the server…"):
- **Why turns went missing:** the Emacs side adds one frame per recorded turn, but skips the update if a frames fetch happens to be running at that moment. A skipped turn was never caught up. Readings that landed during a fetch were lost the same way.
- **Right now:** it has caught up to 36, because this turn's reading landed while it was idle. But that was luck, not the fix.

㊢ (the fix) Two parts:
- **Catch-up after a skip:** a skipped update marks the stepper dirty, and the running fetch refetches as soon as it ends.
- **A 20-second check:** while the stepper is visible and idle, it refetches if it's dirty or if any turn record changed since its last fetch. Record writes are atomic renames, so the store directory's timestamp moves on every write, which makes the check cheap. A full refetch is about 0.9 s of Python, and it only runs when something changed.

The interval is `turn-stepper-reconcile-interval` (0 turns the check off).

㊬ (checked) Four new tests (refetch when dirty, refetch when the store changed, stay quiet when nothing changed, a skipped turn marks dirty) all pass, and all four fail on the previous file. The existing stepper and follow tests still pass (42), and check-parens is OK.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I load it into your Emacs for you (`load-file` on `turn-stepper.el`, plus `session-turn-analysis.el` for the Codex replies from T1)? Or would you rather do it yourself? Until then the 20-second catch-up isn't running.
